answer: The strongest sybil defense prices identity on scarce work history: agents earn payouts only after accumulating verified task completions, each burning real compute in an oasis of reputation surrounded by desert. New identities start at the shale layer with micro-payments per proven task, so mass-registering fakes costs huge compute upfront. Trust compounds slowly, like velvet worn smooth by use, gaining value only through sustained honest labor. Since the payout pool is fixed, mass registration costs more than any payout it could capture, making sybil attacks unprofitable by construction.
